references.text: John 5:18 describes the same reason why the Jews sought to kill Jesus: because he not only broke the Sabbath, but also called God his own Father, which led them to want to take his life.

In John 8:37-40, Jesus repeats that the Jews seek to kill him because there is no place for his word in them, which directly connects to the motive in 7:1 that they had already begun to hunt him down.
John 11:53 shows that the decision to kill Jesus was formalized by the chief priests and Pharisees, explaining why he avoided Judea in 7:1.
John 10:31-33 shows another moment when the Jews picked up stones to stone Jesus, confirming the constant threat of death that forces him to move around in Galilee.
John 12:10-11 shows that the chief priests also planned to kill Lazarus, illustrating the extended conspiracy against Jesus' followers and his own safety situation in Judea.
